# 1.2.116 - the killer unseen until the opening roll, the mask's own "?" on the map and the portrait, Calls on the opening, a hidden token's ruler hidden, every planner node open, the Spectators' room by default and a project action's use limit

An early release, by the owner's decision of 16.11.2026 ("1.2.116 - proponuje wczesniejsze wydanie, tak", and "Etapy
(lub czesci etapow) niewymagajace foundry niech wleca w 1.2.117"). One stage ships: E112 (the opening's veil, the mask's
own "?" and the Loaded Die on the opening). Beside it, four lines merged into the assembly: E112's, owner-116 (the
owner's asks of 15.11.2026), work toward E39 and E40, and work toward E53 and E43. **E39, E40, E43, E53, E58 and E83 are
not shipped**: tools/stages.json plans them for 1.2.117 (commit 271d15c7). The parts of them built here ship as work
toward those stages; what needs a real Foundry - calibration, the performance budget's numbers from a real table, the
local gate and the audit - is not done. E26 stays 1.3.0. From v1.2.115 to 000864a0, the tree before this release
commit: 51 commits, 5 of them merges of the lines into the assembly (`git rev-list --count` and `--merges --count` over
v1.2.115..000864a0).

In plain words:

**The killer is unseen until the opening roll** (E112; the owner, 15.11.2026: "gdy morderca rzuca, dopoki nie rzuci
otwarcia, jego token powinien byc niewidzialny dla ofiary, a sam morderca wyciszony. Dopiero po rzucie odslaniamy
token").
- From the open of a direct murder until its opening roll lands, the primary GM's browser hides the killer's tokens on
  every scene with Foundry's **hidden** and one flag, `flags.danganronpa-rpg.veiled`, which names nobody (mask-gm.mjs
  `veilPatch`). The victim, bystanders and Spectators do not see them; the killer does, and a third already seated on
  the killers' side sees them where the room rule would show them anyway (mask-gm.mjs `veilWanted`, visibility.mjs
  `tokenShownTo`). On a GM's screen the killer's tokens show as hidden, Foundry's own way.
- The killer's microphone is held off, with no silent room: they still hear the room, their voice tile says why
  (`DRPG.Voice.held.veiled`), and they are told so in one line (`DRPG.Veil.card`).
- A murder declared in an Eclipse is veiled as the Eclipse ends, before its lights show anyone (eclipse.mjs `endEclipse`
  calls mask-gm.mjs `veilAtTheLights`, and `lightsJudged` settles the veils once the lights have judged).
- Each token's own **hidden** before the veil is kept in a new GM store, `veils` (gm-stores.mjs `veilStore`), and
  written back exactly when the opening ends: scored, failed, the incident closed, or swept by the primary GM at its
  load or when a primary GM leaves (`settleVeils`). A GM who hides or shows those tokens by hand during the opening is
  undone when the veil lifts: the hidden state written back is the one from before the veil (`liftVeil`). A success that puts the killer behind a "?" puts the "?" on first,
  then shows the token. Closing the roll window does not end the veil: the opening is offered again.
- A veiled killer still counts as in the room - a witness, a Frisk's target, a finder - and keeps their own fog
  (utils.mjs `hiddenByGm`: hidden, but not veiled, where the module read Foundry's hidden as "not in the room").
- A trap and a self-inflicted death veil nobody.
- What it cannot hide, Foundry's limit: a token's **hidden** and its flags reach every browser, so a player's console
  can list the veiled tokens and read whose they are. A new known leak, `foundry-veiled-token-actor` (info), measured
  in scenario 21; the GMs' veil store itself reaches no player (0 rows on the victim's and a bystander's browsers, 1 on
  the GM).

**The mask's own "?", on the map and on the portrait** (E112; the owner, 15.11.2026: "Nie chodzi tylko o portret w
karcie postaci - chodzi tez o ikone tokenu na mapie").
- A killer behind a "?" now wears the module's own question-mark picture, icons/mask-unknown.svg (mask-gm.mjs
  `MASK_IMG`), where Foundry's grey mystery man stood: on the token, its dynamic ring and, new, on the portrait (the
  sheet, the actors' list, the voice tile, a drawn roll's header, the sequence boards). The actor's own picture and its
  prototype token's are kept and given back exactly when the mask ends (`portraitOf`, `portraitBack`). The "?" is
  written to the actor's own picture, so every screen shows it while the mask stands, the GMs' and the killer's own
  sheet too.
- A token made while a mask or the veil stands - dragged from the prototype, or carried to another scene - joins it
  (`adoptToken`, on Foundry's `createToken`); before, the first wore the real picture and the second kept the "?" after
  the end.
- A mask row left standing (restored from a backup, or not ended) no longer stops the next mask: every token it does not
  hold masked is masked, and the portrait too. A token the mask could not write is said on the GM's screen
  (`DRPG.Mask.tokenFailed`), where it was only logged.
- **The masks end before the Class Trial is entered** (clock.mjs `setClock` asks mask-gm.mjs `endMasksBeforeTheBoard`
  before a write that enters the trial). Since 1.2.113 the trial hall's tokens copied the school token's look, so a
  masked killer's hall token was "?" in a trial about who the killer is.
- **And before the start-of-day board**, at the Morning Eclipse's start and at a roll-over (eclipse.mjs `startEclipse`,
  clock.mjs `advanceTimeOfDay`): the board drew no picture in the masked killer's place, which named them by
  elimination (tier 2, red before the fix on both roads).
- Which road showed the owner the real face at a table on 1.2.115 is not known: in the harness 1.2.115's road masked.
  The fixes above answer the two roads the code supports; neither was seen at a table.

**Calls on the murder's opening** (E112; the owner: "loaded die nie zuzywa sie na otwarcie morderstwa", then, to the
question whether the other Calls should reach it, "Inne tez").
- The opening is the murder's own roll and now takes the killer's armed Calls as any action roll does (call-effects.mjs
  `TAKES_CALLS`, "murderOpening"): a Loaded Die loads it, Support and Talent add their dice, a Resolve lets the killer
  pick the statistic if the GM has not picked it yet, and a hindering Call armed on the killer counts too; each is
  spent on it. Measured on 1.2.115's tree before the fix: the packet named no Call, the GM's draw came out 3 and 5, and
  the Loaded Die stayed armed.
- Palm's unseen roll alone still spends no Call (roll-draw.mjs `SPENDS_NO_CALL`, now `{"palm"}`), and, new in this
  release, applies none a packet names: on 1.2.115 the GM's draw applied any armed Call a packet named, a Palm's
  included.

**Smaller E112 changes, on the owner's word of 15.11.2026**
- Isometric Perspective's token silhouettes: with its client setting **Token Silhouette** on, a token this module hides
  on a browser (another room, an Eclipse, the veil) showed its silhouette behind an occluding tile. Each such
  silhouette is now hidden a frame after Isometric draws it (visibility.mjs `hideSilhouettes`); Isometric is not
  edited. Read in Isometric Perspective 14.0.6's source and held on a stand-in stage, not run on a canvas.
- The Infiltrate window lists Keep Watch under Tail Someone: Listen, Echoes, Tail Someone, Keep Watch, Dash, Shut the
  Door, Force the Door, Pick the Lock.
- Tail Someone's and Pick the Lock's hints say what an Eclipse does to them: a tail carries through an Eclipse until the
  day ends and cannot be begun in one; a lock picked and gone through stays open through an Eclipse, and one not yet gone
  through closes at its start. English and Polish.

**A hidden token's movement ruler is hidden too** (owner-116; the owner: "przycisk hide w foundry bazowym (prawy na
token - hide) niech ukrywa tez linie dystansu pokonywanego przez token").
- A token hidden with Foundry's own hide shows no route, waypoints or distance to the players, during the move or
  after. A GM still sees them, and so does the token's owner (the owner's answer of 15.11.2026: at their table a player
  sees their own hidden token). A token the module hides from a player (another room, an Eclipse) hides its ruler from
  them likewise.
- fog-doorways.mjs `HourTokenRuler` asks visibility.mjs `rulerShownTo` on every write of the ruler's `visible`; a
  hide while a ruler stands takes it off at the next ask. The harness has no ruler and no canvas: what is drawn is not
  measured (LIVE-E116-01 to -03).

**The case planner: every node open by default** (owner-116; the owner: "W planerze niech od teraz widok edycji modulu
bedzie domyslnym widokiem modulu", option A).
- **All open**, a new switch in the Map's tools, is on by default: every node shows its fields at once, its kind and
  state on top, with no Close. A node's "Rests on" or "Refutes" list is folded to one line, "Ticked: n of m"; a click
  opens it. Changes are saved when the GM switches to the Table or closes the window. Off, the Map draws each node's
  summary and opens one at a time, as before; the choice is kept on the GM's account.
- Nodes are 300 px wide (were 240), and every field of an open node takes the node's width - the selects under Stained
  Glass too, which were as wide as their words (components.css).
- With every node open the arrow keys walk the open nodes, and the focus after a redraw lands on them, never on a
  hidden summary (case-map.mjs `wireCaseMap`).
- A text field typed in under the Map's zoom keeps its width: the floating field was scaled twice (float-text.mjs
  `holdSize`; at zoom 0.5 a 110 px field floated at 55 px, at zoom 2 a 440 px one at 880 px; now both at their own
  width).
- Measured in Chromium on the module's sheets, not on a table's machine: at Fit to view a case does not fit (the camera
  stops at its least zoom, 0.25, where the smallest text is about 3 px); a column of open nodes is what shows. One
  relayout of 39 open nodes is about 2 ms.

**Spectators talk in the Spectators' room by default** (owner-116; the owner: "Spectatorzy - niech ich pokoj voice chat
bedzie globalny (graczy dalej per room)").
- A Spectator talks in the Spectators' voice channel from anywhere on the map, **with its microphone open**, where it
  was held off by default. **Listen in your room** on its voice tile takes it to hear its token's room, muted, and
  **Talk with the Spectators** brings it back. Students' voices stay per room; during an Eclipse nobody is in voice.
- The old switch's flag (`spectatorTalk`) is read by nothing now: a world holding either of its values keeps its
  Spectators in the Spectators' room. The new one is `spectatorListenHere` (spectator.mjs `SPECTATOR_LISTEN_FLAG`).

**Project actions in Facilities** (work toward E53 and E43; the owner's answers of 15.11.2026).
- **A use limit per character**: in the room action's editor, **Uses** - No limit, Once each time of day, or Once each
  day (the clock's day) - and the Projects window's line names it. A project with none named keeps the rule it had,
  once each time of day (config.mjs `FACILITIES.limits`, `defaultLimit`; facilities.mjs `usedUp`). The primary GM's run
  judges each use by it ("used already today" under Once each day). The editor's opening line, which said "once per
  character each time of day" whatever the choice, now points to **Uses** (`DRPG.Facility.editor.projectIntro`,
  English and Polish).
- Each player's browser now holds its own characters' uses (facility-uses.mjs, the copy `facilityUseCopy`), so the
  Facilities window greys a used action with its reason. The uses are now in the case's backup (`facilityUseStore`,
  `backup: true`), and the copies are sent again after a restore.
- A secret project's room action stays in the Facilities of those in on it after the chat log is cleared: it rides the
  GMs' sight copy (projects.mjs `sightFor`, `receiveSight`), where it rode only a GM's private card. Which road was the
  owner's own case at the table is still not known.
- A sealed repair's completion card named its secret target by the GMs' name to every reader of the repair (E43-F11,
  medium: a player given the repair alone read the target's name). Now each reader gets a card with the name they may
  read (projects-secrecy.mjs `nameAs` behind projects.mjs `projectLabel(id, user)`); that player reads "Work on ???
  can resume."

**What the table's own work costs, and the balance log** (work toward E53).
- `game.drpg.perf()` gives a roll's round trip as p50 and p95 beside the slowest (it gave the median), and a new block:
  what the table's own work cost on that browser, each line with its count - a student's or a Remnant's ring drawn
  again, the fog repainted, the case dashboard rebuilt, a chat card painted, the canvas drawn on a change of scene
  (into the trial hall and out of it) and, on the primary GM, the audit of a sheet write (perf-timings.mjs,
  diagnostics.mjs `costLines`). Nothing is made to happen for the report: a line reads "none since this browser
  loaded" until the table has done that thing.
- **The balance log records the rolls**, a new world setting in the settings window's Rules, **off by default**. While
  on, the primary GM keeps every action roll it draws for a player in a GM store (`balanceLog`, in the case's backup, cut
  by no reset); `game.drpg.balanceNote(text)` adds a GM's note, and `game.drpg.balanceReport()` reads each action
  against the exact count of the dice (the 144 throws of 2d12). It records only: no rule number changes. Nothing clears
  the log yet. docs/dev/balance.md says what it holds and which questions to bring back from sessions 0.

**Work toward E39 and E40** (meant to change nothing at the table).
- One rule for whether a road is open in the phase: scripts/allowed-now.mjs `allowedNow(actor, key, { road, facts })`
  answers `{ ok, why, road }`, `why` one of `WHY` (eclipse, trial, incident, murderOnlyInEclipse), over five roads
  (action, person, transfer, passageShare, passageFind). The sheet's tile, the press, the person roads (frisk.mjs
  `personActionRefusal`), the rifle's transfer (inventory.mjs) and the passages' show and search (passages-gm.mjs) ask
  it, each in its own order and its own words as before. Read in the code, not run: the tile's sentence differs from
  before only where an Eclipse stands with a fight or the trial, which the module does not reach.
- A chat card that is gone ends nothing: an ask card deleted before its expiry fired about five minutes later and read the
  GMs' stores (call-gm.mjs `cardGone`, in `endExpired` and `endSentOn`). Found as an order dependence between tier-2
  tests; it was on main too.
- The harness's world scan lets a setting that holds a row for every actor alike stand (world-secrets.mjs
  `uniformActorRows`, for `diceLookWorld`); a watched actor's id anywhere else is still found. Found when 18-trial
  reloaded the GM: red on 1.2.115's tree too, read as no leak.
- Scenario 18-trial grew from 26 checks to 91: a second trial with "Nobody is executed", the Final Trial, a late player
  with the "your vote is in" notice, a GM's reload in the vote, and a season reset during a suicide incident, with the
  player leak scans after each step.

## Before installing

- **No world migration.** Four settings are added (`game.settings.register` on 198 lines of scripts/ at v1.2.115, 202
  at 271d15c7): one world setting, **The balance log records the rolls** (`balanceLog`, off by default), and three
  client stores no player sets by hand (`gmVeils`, `gmBalanceLog`, `mineFacilityUses`). None is removed. The GMs'
  stores go from 64 definitions to 66 (`veils`, `balanceLog`) and the player copies from 15 to 16 (`facilityUses`);
  the old stores keep their keys.
- **Project actions**: a project saved before this release has no use limit named and reads Once each time of day, the
  rule it had. The room action uses are now in the case's backup; a backup made on 1.2.115 has none.
- **A mask row of 1.2.115** kept no portrait: the next mask over it keeps the portrait first, then masks it.
- **Spectators**: every Spectator talks in the Spectators' room with its microphone open after the update, whatever its
  old switch said.
- **Language**: lang/en.json goes from 6335 to 6356 keys: 21 added, none removed, 5 changed in wording (Tail Someone's
  and Pick the Lock's hints, the Spectator's button, the room action uses' store label
  `DRPG.Case.store.facilityUses`, the room action editor's opening line `DRPG.Facility.editor.projectIntro`), counted on the flattened files, v1.2.115 against 000864a0. lang/pl.json goes from 7420 to 7441: every English key and no other but
  the Polish plural forms (.few, .many; 532, as before) and the 553 DRPG.Config.* keys (same count).
- One icon is added (icons/mask-unknown.svg). The console gains `game.drpg.balanceReport()` and
  `game.drpg.balanceNote(text)` (tools/api-surface.json: two names added, none removed).
- **Daggerheart**: `verified` stays 2.12.8; Foundry's stays 14.365 (module.json's compatibility has no change).

## Repository

- Tests, 17 new registry rows: R7405-R7408 (E112), R7520-R7527 (owner-116), R7540-R7543 (E53 and E43), R7560 (E40);
  all stamped E112, the stage that ships them (271d15c7); next free R7561. New tier-2 tests by name: eight "E112 - ..."
  (the veil, the Calls on the opening, a Resolve's picker, the portrait, an adopted token, the start-of-day board, the
  masks before the Class Trial), E40-T4, E40-T5, E53-T1 and "owner-116: the planner draws every node open by default";
  E40-T3 extended.
- Changed on purpose, among others: R3755 and R3756 (the Infiltrate rows' order), R3860, R7168 and R3853 (the
  Spectator's flag), R5821 (the node's width), R4755 (the Case tooltips' keys), R1157 (the folded list's ratio), R42
  (the shared rule), R553 (a census row for E112's new token hook), eight tier-2 tests whose subject is a node's Close (they ask the one-node drawing),
  scenario 93's `voice` and `talk` checks.
- Scenarios extended: 18-trial (above), 21-masked-killer (the owner's road and the veil read from a console), 72-canary
  (a sealed repair's end), 93-spectator, 99-actions (the use limits).
- **On the E53 line before its merge**, found by that line's own shard run on 592fcff0: the backup test's fixtures for
  `balanceLog` and `facilityUses`, perf()'s trip line read as p50, and scenario 13 (725b4097).
- **CI fixes on the assembly**: scenario 30's mask check reads `MASK_IMG` from mask-gm.mjs, where it held Foundry's mystery
  man by path (9b1f0183; CI 43810162456 on 88ed05b3 was red in bucket b2 on it); scenario 95 no longer holds the node
  Close's tooltip, which an open-all Map does not draw, and holds five keys it found drawn (the Map's All open switch
  and folded list, the planner's Clear, a project's scale and a secret project's player tick). Three more it found
  drawn alone - the trial's edit, delete and Monokuma's confirm - were not drawn in CI's bucket b2 after 30, 69 and 86
  (CI 43819231988 on 9b1f0183), so they are not held (87f1f08d).
- **A113-C5-7-T1, 1.2.115's unexplained CI red, explained and fixed** (e4878dff, the test only): it sorted the rows it
  read with `localeCompare` and the rows it expected by code units; with Foundry's mixed-case ids the two orders
  disagree on about 18% of random pairs. One comparator on both sides now, and fixed ids that sort apart, so a mismatch
  is red on every run.
- Tools: `node tools/check.mjs budget` (tools/perf-budget.mjs) holds audit/perf-baseline.json's new `budget` to every
  run a table measured; every threshold is null until the owner gives one, and while `runs` is empty each line prints
  "not measured". audit/perf-baseline.json has a `perfFunction` revision for E53, written for 1.2.116; audit/live/
  perf-baseline.mjs reads the new perf() lines. audit/case-map-sweep.mjs reads and plants on the open fields too;
  audit/float-sweep.mjs I7 reads the floating field under the zoom.
- The handbooks (GM and player, English and Polish), README's privacy paragraph (the veil's leak) and
  audit/AUDIT-1.2.42.md 9.2, items 553-561 (LIVE-E112-01 to -05, LIVE-E116-01 to -03, LIVE-E53-01).

## Known gaps

- **Not shipped**: E39, E40, E43, E53, E58 and E83 (tools/stages.json, planned 1.2.117); E58 and E83 had no work here.
  Of E53, the budget's numbers wait for a run at a table (LIVE-E53-01, LIVE-E33-05); `runs` is empty, so the budget
  holds nothing yet. E26 stays 1.3.0.
- **Defaults taken, each to confirm**: a closed roll window keeps the veil; Spectators do not see a veiled token; a
  Spectator's microphone is open by default in the Spectators' room. When a GM other than the primary ends an Eclipse,
  the killer is veiled at the open, a moment later (read off the code, not driven).
- **Read and left**: the verdict's cut-in draws a masked killer sentenced there as an initial, after the card has named
  them (cosmetic, the coordinator's word); a Daggerheart chat card written before the mask keeps the face (not read in
  Daggerheart's source); whether a frame of a silhouette shows before it is hidden (LIVE-E112-05);
  docs/handbook-facts.player-handbook.en.json and its brochure twin quote the old order of the Infiltrate rows (left for
  E57's next pass of the facts files).
- **A roomless project's action** stays unavailable where a character stands in no room (the owner's decision of
  15.11.2026: no change).
- **Not moved onto the shared rule**: the Calls' own phase gates, the Monocub's abilities, the handover and a statistic
  proposal's gate (each named in docs/dev/e40/STATUS.md); and 18-trial does not yet hold duplicates on the card,
  preselection, D4's offer applied once, a deceased before and after discovery or season-wipe on a world copy.
- **Measured nowhere at a table**: the planner's first draw with every node open, and Foundry's own stylesheet under it;
  the cost of the ruler's rule during a drag; the balance log over a session (it has recorded none).
- **Carried from 1.2.115, not closed**: a killer behind a "?" keeps their token's actor (known leak
  `foundry-masked-token-actor`); 72-canary's three expected reds (`foundry-hidden-tokens`, `foundry-actor-items`,
  `S17-64`).
